thread:
rita: Heads-up: we're seeing a preempt cascade in us-west2-rack-C. Large training pods keep getting preempted as tiny inference jobs immediately bind to freed GPUs. Saw ~120 preempts in 10m.
omar: Confirming. Scheduler traces show repeated relocate attempts and solver thrash. Also noticed a node-label rip where `gpu-type:v2` got changed to `gpu-type:v2a` by label-syncer during a rollout 30m ago. That broken label caused many pods with `nodeAffinity: gpu-type=v2` to become unschedulable and triggered preempt/rebind churn.
lee: Logs:```
I0505 15:02:11 preempt.go:76] Preempting pod ml-large-2024-83 on node node-west2c-07
I0505 15:02:11 solver.go:192] placement search depth=8 combinations=2.1e6 mem=2.2GB
I0505 15:02:12 solver.go:205] allocation failed: runtime: out of memory
I0505 15:02:12 scheduler.go:310] fallback to heuristic -> immediate bind tiny-infer-* to preempted node
```
tori: So two problems: label drift making many existing pods unschedulable, and immediate greedy binding of new tiny jobs to just-freed GPUs.
omar: Immediate mitigations I propose: 1) pause label-syncer rollout and revert label patch, 2) add a short preemption cooldown (e.g. 30s) so nodes just freed don't accept new best-effort pods for a bit, 3) temporarily increase scheduler memory cap or reduce search depth to avoid OOM.
rita: Can we throttle the queue of tiny jobs? Maybe webhook to mark ephemeral jobs as `preempt-priority=low` and delay scheduling by 15s.
lee: Quick commands: revert label-syncer deployment: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/label-syncer -n infra`
--- apply scheduler arg canary: `kubectl -n infra patch deployment scheduler --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kube-scheduler","args":["--placement-search-depth=4"]}]}}}}'`
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-8421 severity=high assigned=eng-platform.
rita: After reverting label-syncer and applying search-depth canary, preempt rate fell to ~12 in 10m (was 120). Node drain backlog cleared in ~14m.
omar: Follow-ups: - audit label-syncer rollout validation (prevent label renames that break affinity) - add scheduler metric for "recently-freed node cooldown" to avoid greedy binds - add a fallback soft-affinity for `gpu-type` so pods can tolerate small naming diffs for a short window.
tori: Cost note: packing ephemeral tiny jobs onto freshly freed GPUs improved short-term utilization but caused wasted recompute. Finance flagged potential +8% burn for this pattern if not addressed.
rita: I'll open the postmortem + config diffs and assign remediation tickets. For now leaving the search-depth canary in ap-west for 1h. :thumbsup:
